lead: # Source-experience stage: inventory / sample / infer-model / persist-model commands.
# Enabled by default; disable with --no-default-features for builds that exclude the
# data-platform source commands (e.g. minimal CI builds).
# GRAPH MATERIALIZATION, as a real build-dependency
# (`graph-materialize-becomes-a-real-build-dependency`). A package gets exactly ONE build script and
# this one already has its own doing four jobs, so the `build = "../graph-materialize/build.rs"` line
# the other 54 crates use is not available here — the shared file has to be CALLED instead. `build.rs`
# runs it as a fifth job. NOTE this manifest still has no `build` key: cargo auto-detects `build.rs`,
# which is why the collision was invisible to anyone diffing manifests.
# The skills + MCP resolution, moved out of this binary so a pure decision over serde-able data
# stops costing a rebuild and a restarted window (the-resolution-decisions-live-in-the-app-binary-not-a-crate).
# The session PERMISSION DERIVATION, moved out of `src-tauri/src/session/` so that changing which
# commands a role may run no longer costs a new binary and a restarted window (#the-session-permission-derivation-lives-in-a-crate-not-src-tauri).
# The store projections a sandboxed session reads instead of running `bsc` (which would mean
# binding a writable database into the cage). See `project_stores_for`.
# Layered-DAG layout, O(V+E) and index-based — 1M nodes / 2M edges in 256 ms. Dependency-free leaf
# crate, so it adds nothing to the app's build beyond itself.
# Single-instance guard (#1303): a second launch focuses the running window instead of
# spawning a duplicate process. Desktop-only.
# `std` enables `set_boxed_logger` for the custom `GraphLogger` (#1389) — previously pulled in
# transitively by `tauri-plugin-log`, which we replaced.
# The prompt-injection scanner (`planner::injection_scan`) ports seven JavaScript regexes, and a
# hand-rolled matcher would be exactly the second parser that port exists to remove. Already in
# Cargo.lock via bsc-agent and llm, so this adds an edge, not a new external dependency.
# FCM push to the paired mobile app (#846): service-account OAuth2 needs an RS256-signed
# JWT assertion. `jsonwebtoken` reads the service-account PEM private key directly and
# signs the assertion; the access-token exchange + the FCM v1 POST reuse `reqwest`.
# Mobile tunnel (#242): the desktop ⇄ mobile bridge runs over a zero-knowledge
# relay (#241), end-to-end encrypted with Noise IK so the relay only ever sees
# ciphertext. `snow` is the Noise implementation (pure-Rust default resolver — no
# system crypto toolchain); `tokio` runs the relay client; `tokio-tungstenite`
# dials the relay over real (CA-signed) TLS via rustls + webpki roots; `base64`
# encodes the static public key for the pairing QR; `rand` mints room ids + PSKs.
# PKCE (#1197 OAuth): SHA-256 of the verifier for the S256 code challenge.
# rustls 0.23 won't auto-select a CryptoProvider at runtime unless its provider
# feature is pinned, so the relay dial's first TLS handshake panics the tunnel
# thread. Pin `ring` and install it as the process default at startup (lib.rs `run`).
# Performance monitoring (#569): sysinfo samples per-agent process RSS/CPU cheaply
# (only tracked PIDs, no full system walk); rusqlite persists the time-series.
# `bundled` compiles SQLite from source for cross-platform reliability.
# Shared leaf utilities (#1646): the ONE home-dir / `~/.base-studio-code` resolver, so the app
# and every `bsc-*` CLI agree on which on-disk store they read/write. `platform/paths.rs`
# delegates `home_dir`/`bsc_base_dir` here.
# The imagination feed model + its on-disk format; the app only READS it.
# The GitHub REST/GraphQL transport, extracted so `bsc` can reach it too
# (`extract-a-tauri-free-github-transport-crate`). `github/api.rs` is now thin shims over this.
# `bsc shot` (#3261): the request/response protocol the CLI and this watcher share. Tauri-free by
# design — only the platform capture lives app-side.
# The ONE bsc→app request channel + the navigate verb (#3274, epic #3260).
# The app subscribes to the sensor's stream itself (src/lan/subscribe.rs): the
# webview cannot bind a UDP socket, and putting the group key inside it would
# be worse if it could.
# Real fleet liveness over the shared channel (#4098) — the app owns PtyState, so only it can answer.
# The `bsc persona use` wire contract (#change-a-panes-persona-from-the-cli). The pane->persona map is
# frontend state, so the app supplies only the emit-and-ack; the crate supplies the shapes.
# Read-only inspection of the live view answered by the appchan watcher (#3437).
# The app-owned SYSTEM SESSIONS' closed registry + lifecycle contract
# (#architect-starts-and-stops-system-sessions). The app re-resolves every id against it, so the
# closed set is a boundary rather than a CLI-side convention.
# PNG decode/encode for the --rect crop (CapturePreview hands back the WHOLE webview). `png` not
# `image`: it is the only format CapturePreview emits, and it keeps the binary off a codec matrix.
# Unified log engine (#1607/#1389): the pure scope-graph policy (`logs::scope`) shared by the desktop
# `GraphLogger` and the `bsc log` CLI, so one config type + one matching rule govern both surfaces.
# Data platform (#781/#784): the canonical Data Model store (DuckDB) + connector
# framework. Pulling this in compiles bundled DuckDB into the desktop build.
# On-device credential store for migration source connectors (#1194): secrets go to the OS
# keychain (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain), never to the plan config or the planner.
# Per-project plan store (#plan-db) — shared with the `bsc-plan` agent CLI. The Tauri
# commands below are a thin wrapper over this crate's `Store`.
# Per-project runtime-fault store (#2258/#2260) — shared with the `bsc errors` agent CLI. The
# localhost fault-ingest collector (#2261, `observability::collector`) resolves each project's
# error.db and calls this crate's `Store::record` to land fingerprinted runtime faults.
# Runtime-attestation store (#runtime-attests-what-actually-ran) — `observability::attest` folds
# the frontend's batched "which record actually served this module" rows into runtime.db, which
# `bsc runtime` and `doctor` read back through this same crate.
# Lightweight, synchronous, pure-Rust HTTP server (#2261). The fault-ingest collector runs one
# `tiny_http` receiver bound to 127.0.0.1 on a background thread — no async runtime, no framework,
# just the loopback POST endpoint the generated app's fault shim reports to.
# Mobile-tunnel wire contract + Noise crypto (#1919) — desktop tunnel glue (state/transport/commands) depends on it.
# The keychain-backed Vault the tunnel's durable pairing SEED is stored through
# (one-pairing-assigns-every-room). The app used to mint a room and psk per dial, so restarting
# it unpaired the phone BY DESIGN; pairing once requires the seed to outlive the process.
# Reached as a trait object, so the decision is testable against an in-memory fake. `keyring` is
# already a direct dependency for the sources/credentials path — this is deliberately NOT that:
# bsc-secret carries the write-then-read-back guard, and on Linux a missing Secret Service makes
# keyring accept every write and forget it, which would report a pairing as durable when it is not.
# Cross-project hub lifecycle (#1720) — shared with the `bsc-project` session CLI. The
# published-marker helpers (`mark_published`/`is_published`/`published_marker`) delegate here so
# the `.published` marker logic lives in ONE place (#1761).
# Global skills + task-groups store (#1338, instance of #1325) — shared with the `bsc skill`
# session CLI. The desktop Skills library reaches this store through the generic `bsc` command
# (`bsc skill …`, #2142), so the UI and every live console session read/write ONE global skills.db.
# Model-agnostic LLM provider layer (#1097) — shared with the future lean `bsc-agent`
# binary so neither has to depend on the other. `llm_complete` dispatches through it.
# NOTE: the desktop no longer depends on the `logs` crate directly (#2144). The observability READS
# that used to call into it (token-cost pricing, per-pane activity/done rollups, raw stream tails)
# now route through the `bsc logs` CLI over the `bsc` bridge — the engine lives in `crates/logs` and
# is reached as the bundled `bsc` binary, not linked in. The in-crate `observability::logs` module
# (user-facing log inventory/clear/export + `read_log_tail`) is unrelated and stays.
# The algorithms knowledge graph (#4078) — LINKED (was dev-only) so `graph_dump` reads the store
# IN-PROCESS. The Algorithms page polls it every 5s, and routing that through the `bsc` bridge spawned
# a subprocess per tick just to learn the graph had not changed; the same mistake #3630 and #4074
# fixed for the log pollers. Linking the real crate (rather than reading the JSON with bare `std::fs`)
# keeps ONE store-path resolver — `BSC_GRAPH_STORE`, else `~/.base-studio-code/knowledge/…` — so the
# app and the CLI cannot drift onto different files.
# It ALSO still backs the test below (#3391): the packaged librarian spec (`data/librarian/claude.md`)
# TEACHES the `bsc graph` CLI, so its content test derives the expected verb/flag surface from
# `bsc_graph::cli::{VERBS, IMPL_SUBVERBS, FLAGS}` instead of a second hand-written list.
# The record LEDGER, queried directly by the four graph commands — the page's index, the resolver's
# feed, one record's source, and the change signature are four different questions, and a database can
# answer each without materialising the others.
# `vendored::sha256_hex` — the ONE content-hash form in this workspace, for `graph_sig`. Already in this
# crate's tree transitively (bsc-graph depends on it), so the direct edge costs nothing at build time
# and buys not having a second spelling of "the hash of this thing" that can drift from the first.
# The session-memory store, read IN-PROCESS at launch like plandb and bsc-graph beside it — so
#  needs no subprocess. Tauri-free and DuckDB-free; this edge costs nothing.
# The COMPONENT library, so a feature's `requires` resolves in EITHER graph (#requires-names-components).
# DuckDB-free, like bsc-graph beside it — this edge costs nothing at build time.
# Unix-only: process-group signalling so a PTY's whole tree (shell + claude + any
# grandchildren) dies with the session on pty_kill / app exit. portable-pty calls
# `setsid()` in the spawned shell, so the shell leads a process group whose pgid ==
# its pid; `killpg(pgid, SIGKILL)` reaches every descendant that didn't re-setsid.
# Without it, `portable_pty::Child::kill()` only terminates the immediate shell and
# leaves `claude` (and any `gh`/`git` it spawned) orphaned, holding cwd locks.
sections.name: [target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]

lead: # Linux capture (`bsc shot`): the app runs on WebKitGTK here, and `webkit_web_view_get_snapshot` is the
# sibling of the Windows `CapturePreview` — a RENDER of the webview, not an OS window grab. Both crates
# are already in the tree via tauri/wry; declaring them makes them reachable, and pins `cairo-rs` to the
# version webkit2gtk hands back from the snapshot callback so the two `Surface` types are one type.
# `png` is cairo's own encoder (`Surface::write_to_png`, gated behind that feature). Encoding by hand
# from the surface bytes instead would mean undoing cairo's PREMULTIPLIED alpha on ARGB32 — a real
# correctness trap for no gain, since cairo ships the encoder for exactly this.
sections.name: [target.'cfg(target_os = "linux")'.dependencies]

lead: # `bsc shot` (#3261): the WebView2 snapshot. `CapturePreview` renders the webview's COMPOSITED output —
# pixel-identical to what the user sees, including the sandboxed preview iframe, and immune to
# occlusion/minimize/screen-lock (an OS window grab is not). Both crates are already in the tree via
# Tauri; pinned to the versions it resolves so we never link two `windows` majors.
# `Com_StructuredStorage` for CreateStreamOnHGlobal (the capture sink); `Foundation` for the HGLOBAL
# it takes. Pinned to the version Tauri already resolves so we never link two `windows` majors.
# (Dependabot's 0.61 → 0.62 bump, #3446, broke this — Tauri/webview2-com still resolve 0.61, so 0.62
# split our COM types (IStream/HGLOBAL/core::Result in shot/mod.rs) from webview2-com's. Do NOT bump
# ahead of a Tauri/wry bump that moves the whole tree to 0.62.)
# Windows-only: Job Object APIs so a PTY's whole process tree (shell + claude +
# any grandchildren) dies with the session on pty_kill / app exit. Without this,
# `portable_pty::Child::kill()` only terminates the immediate shell and leaves
# `claude` (and any `gh`/`git` it spawned) orphaned, holding cwd locks.
sections.name: [target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]

lead: # THE MODULE-ID DERIVATION, so `testutil::module_source` never restates it
# (`three-src-tauri-modules-read-their-own-source`). This crate's self-scanning guards resolve a module
# through the materialized `$OUT_DIR/crate.rs` once it is a record, and the section they want is named
# by the id `graph-materialize` DERIVED when it emitted it. A second copy of that derivation here could
# disagree with what was actually written, and the guard would report a module missing that is right
# there. It is already a `[build-dependencies]` entry above, so nothing new is compiled for the host.
